newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Iraqis seek asylum in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Iraqis seek asylum in Australia.

text.p: A group of Iraqis are seeking political asylyum in Australia after escaping from their troubled homeland, a government official said on Monday.
The immigration department official told Reuters the Australian government was considering the 36 Iraqis' asylum applications, but did not know when a decision would be made.
Australian media reports said on Monday the group fled Iraq overland to Jordan before flying to Malaysia, using fake passports.

They then travelled through Indonesia and paid Indonesian smugglers to drop them on a barren island off Australia's northern coast, where they were found by an Australian navy patrol, the reports said.
The Iraqis, believed to be professionals such as doctors and lawyers fearing persecution in their homeland, arrived by several boats in September and October.
It is rare for refugees from outside Asia to arrive in Australia by boat. Most boatpeople are from neighbouring countries such as China and Vietnam.
The last arrival from outside the region was a boatload of 12 Poles in 1992.
